---
title: "Alter and update table schemas"
description: "Modify the schema of an existing hypertable with the ALTER TABLE command in PostgreSQL"
products: [cloud, self_hosted]
---

import * as C from "@constants";
import { Callout } from "@stainless-api/docs/components";
import { NumberedList, NumberedItem } from "@components/NumberedList";

Schema changes on a {C.HYPERTABLE} use normal {C.PG} `ALTER TABLE` syntax, and {C.TIMESCALE_DB} propagates those changes to every underlying {C.CHUNK}.

<Callout variant="note">

Schema changes to a {C.CAGG} are limited. You can rename the view or its
columns, set a schema, change the owner, and adjust parameters. Since
{C.TIMESCALE_DB} 2.28.0, you can also add a new aggregate with
[`ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW ... ADD COLUMN`](/reference/timescaledb/continuous-aggregates/alter_materialized_view).
Other schema changes are not supported.

</Callout>

For example, to add a new column called `address` to a table called `distributors`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE distributors
  ADD COLUMN address varchar(30);
```

This creates the new column, with all existing entries recording `NULL` for the
new column.

Changing the schema can, in some cases, consume a lot of resources. This is
especially true if it requires underlying data to be rewritten. If you want to
check your schema change before you apply it, you can use a `CHECK` constraint,
like this:

```sql
ALTER TABLE distributors
  ADD CONSTRAINT zipchk
  CHECK (char_length(zipcode) = 5);
```

This scans the table to verify that existing rows meet the constraint, but does
not require a table rewrite.

## Altering {C.HYPERTABLE}s with {C.COLUMNSTORE} enabled

Most common schema modifications work on {C.HYPERTABLE}s with {C.COLUMNSTORE} enabled, including adding
columns, renaming columns, dropping columns, adding constraints, setting NOT NULL,
and changing defaults. However, some operations are blocked, the most common of them being:

- **Changing column data type** (`ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE`)
- **Changing column storage** (`ALTER COLUMN ... SET STORAGE`)
- **Dropping orderby or segmentby columns**
- **Row-level security operations** (`ENABLE/DISABLE ROW SECURITY`)

When you attempt a blocked operation, you receive an error:

```
ERROR: operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled
```

If you encounter this error, you need to:

1. Stop any {C.COLUMNSTORE} policy
2. Convert the affected {C.CHUNK}s back into {C.ROWSTORE}
3. Disable {C.COLUMNSTORE}
4. Perform the schema change
5. Re-enable {C.COLUMNSTORE} and restart the policy

### Example: change the column type on a {C.HYPERTABLE} with {C.COLUMNSTORE} enabled

This example shows how to change a column's data type on a {C.HYPERTABLE} with
{C.COLUMNSTORE} enabled, which requires conversion to {C.ROWSTORE}:

<NumberedList>

<NumberedItem title="Check if you have a columnstore policy and note its settings">

Query the jobs catalog to find the `job_id` and configuration for any existing {C.COLUMNSTORE} policy:

```sql
SELECT job_id, config FROM timescaledb_information.jobs
WHERE proc_name = 'policy_compression'
  AND hypertable_name = 'conditions';
```

</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Pause the columnstore policy">

If a policy exists, pause it so it does not convert {C.CHUNK}s while you are modifying the schema:

```sql
SELECT alter_job(<job_id>, scheduled => false);
```

</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Convert all ${C.CHUNK}s back to ${C.ROWSTORE}`}>

Use [`convert_to_rowstore`](/reference/timescaledb/hypercore/convert_to_rowstore) to move each {C.CHUNK} out of the {C.COLUMNSTORE}:

```sql
DO $$ DECLARE chunk regclass;
BEGIN
  FOR chunk IN SELECT show_chunks('conditions') LOOP
    CALL convert_to_rowstore(chunk);
  END LOOP;
END $$;
```

</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Disable ${C.COLUMNSTORE}`}>

Some operations, such as changing a column type, require {C.COLUMNSTORE} to be fully disabled:

```sql
ALTER TABLE conditions SET (timescaledb.columnstore = false);
```

</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Perform the schema modification">

```sql
ALTER TABLE conditions
  ALTER COLUMN temperature TYPE double precision;
```

</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Re-enable ${C.COLUMNSTORE} with original settings`}>

```sql
ALTER TABLE conditions SET (
  timescaledb.columnstore = true,
  timescaledb.orderby = 'time DESC',
  timescaledb.segmentby = 'device_id'
);
```

</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Restart the columnstore policy">

```sql
SELECT alter_job(<job_id>, scheduled => true);
```

</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Optionally, convert ${C.CHUNK}s to ${C.COLUMNSTORE} immediately`}>

Without this step, {C.CHUNK}s are converted by the policy on its next scheduled run. To convert them now, use
[`convert_to_columnstore`](/reference/timescaledb/hypercore/convert_to_columnstore):

```sql
DO $$ DECLARE chunk regclass;
BEGIN
  FOR chunk IN SELECT show_chunks('conditions') LOOP
    CALL convert_to_columnstore(chunk);
  END LOOP;
END $$;
```

</NumberedItem>

</NumberedList>

For more information about {C.PG} `ALTER TABLE` operations, see the
[{C.PG} `ALTER TABLE` documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-altertable.html).
